newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down after low tender award.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down after low tender award.

text.p: Gasoline in Singapore fell on strong selling pressure as the market reacted to the low award by Taiwan of its buying tender and a sharply weaker crude market, traders said on Thursday.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought one more unleaded 95-octane reformate at the same $27.40 per barrel it paid for a cargo it bought on Wednesday.
CPC also bought a leaded 95-octane reformate cargo at $27.70 per barrel cost-and-freight in the tender, a CPC official said.
The tender which closed April 1 and is valid for two days, required the three 250,000-barrel cargoes to be delivered to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung in the first half of May.
The awards were sharply lower than CPC's previous award, when it bought a leaded cargo at $29.00 for April 1-15 delivery and unleaded reformate at a much higher $28.60 April 16-30 arrival.

Also, overnight May Brent crude lost a hefty 60 cents to close at $18.51 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange and lost further ground on Thursday to last trade down 15 cents to $18.36 in London at 1110 GMT.
In the physical market a European major sold to a Japanese trader 50,000-barrels of 95-octane unleaded loading April 29-May 3 at $27.30 per barrel, free-on-board Singapore.
The deal is well under the $27.50 and $27.70 deals that were recorded on Wednesday for lifting April 26-30 and 17-21, respectively, both to the same Japanese trader.
The Japanese buyer, who had already bought one million barrels in March and so far bought 250,000 barrels in April.
A major said that the market was well supplied with exports to the region even seen from Yanbu.
